name: Gallium
occurrence: Rare and dispersed, found in trace amounts within zinc and aluminium ores.
majorUses: LEDs and semiconductors (gallium arsenide, gallium nitride)
notableCharacteristics: Melts at just below body temperature (29.8°C), so it turns to liquid metal sitting in your hand.
whyHere: Its melting point sits far below neighbouring metals because its crystal structure bonds atoms in pairs rather than a dense uniform lattice, leaving unusually weak overall bonding for a metal.
didYouKnow: Gallium was one of the elements Mendeleev predicted before its discovery, matching his 'eka-aluminium' prediction so precisely that he even corrected the density measurement of the actual discovered sample.
genZNote: Melts in your hand like a magic trick. Also secretly running your 5G phone signal.
